title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: No new close since Friday — Nasdaq fell 2.1% on renewed AI-spending jitters (CoreWeave -11.9% on the day, -23% for the week); S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures were last pointing sharply lower (-1.1%, -2.5%) heading into today's open.
Markets: 10-year Treasury yield near 5.1% (off last week's 5.3% high); Brent crude near $110/bbl, highest since May, on supply/inflation worries; gold ~$4,189/oz, bitcoin ~$81.6k.
Companies: Tesla shares slipped 2.1% after a cool reception to its SpaceX-thruster Roadster reveal; Barclays analysts flag a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger as soon as this fall.
Companies: CoreWeave's multiday stock-and-debt selloff continues to rattle AI-infrastructure names as investors question returns on AI capex.

Companies: Apple and Meta struck a rare AI truce — Meta's open-weight 'Muse Spark Open' model will run locally on Apple's M5 Ultra Mac Studios; separately, Broadcom and Verizon are pushing back on the SEC's stock-tokenization plans.

Macro/Policy: Wall Street is growing wary of the AI buildout — Gartner sees $7T in AI infrastructure spend through 2030 vs. only $3.6T in resulting revenue, and AI-debt issuance plunged to $23B in September from $113B in June as banks (JPMorgan included) pull back.
Macro/Policy: Week ahead — September housing starts due Tuesday, with Meta and Tesla reporting Q3 earnings Wednesday as earnings season ramps up.
